doc.title: Al Tinney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Closing remarks
summary: The interview ends as tape runs out; Tinney appreciates being asked about his family and says it is not only the music.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing the interview: thanks, goodbyes and tape running out

blocks.x: Well it’s really been fascinating talking with you today.
You know we might have to do another part here sometime because you’ve got so much to say.
Okay. Well this is the end of it like?
Well we’re running out of tape.
Okay. I’m running out too, so everything turned out all right. It turned out beautiful. I enjoyed this.
Well thank you for your time I really appreciate it.

I don’t know if you were looking for something educational, which I’m not really a clinical person. So I’m glad you asked me about my life and you did ask me about children and grandchildren. No one else does this.
It’s not just the music as you said.
Right. It’s not only the music.
